>

wait_until translates into trap > wait > untrap, and does not handle
priorities at all. Entities arriving there follow a simple FIFO order
when a signal is received. The problem (the first one and this second
one when you add priorities) has to do with simultaneous events.
simmer does its best to try to get them right, but if you have so many
times happening at the same time (in this case, a release from A + a
release from B + arrivals waiting), there's no way to cover all
possible cases.

If your final simulation has random delays and generation patterns (or
at least they are not integers or multiples), your problems will most
probably disappear, and you won't even need the prioritization
function. Nonetheless, I would try this one simpler approach (note
that queue_size=Inf for the "B token" this time):

library(simmer)

interleaved_resources <- function(.trj, names, delays) {
  for (i in seq_along(names)) {
    .trj %>%
      seize(names[i]) %>%
      timeout(delays[i])
    if (i < length(names)) .trj %>%

      seize(paste(names[i+1], "token"))

    .trj %>%
      release(names[i])
    if (i > 1) .trj %>%
      release(paste(names[i], "token"))
  }
  .trj
}

t <- trajectory() %>%

  interleaved_resources(c("A", "B"), c(2, 3))

simmer() %>%
  add_resource("A", 2, Inf) %>%
  add_resource("B", 2, 1) %>%
  add_resource("B token", 3, Inf) %>%
  add_generator("dummy", t, function() 0.5) %>%
  run(20) %>%
  get_mon_arrivals()

Please, let me know if this works.

messages.subject_clean: help getting started: clinical trial enrollment simulation
messages.body_plain:
It's clear simmer has all the pieces I need to put this together, but it's all new, so a pointer or two would be appreciated.

An overly simplified clinical trial enrollment simulation consists of a known number of "sites", each with 1) a known "start" time (not stochastic, at least for now) and 2) an expected average rate of patient enrollment (e.g. 1 patient/week), specific for each site (again, treated as known at this point, not stochastic). Once a site has started, they enroll patients as a Poisson process according to their rate. I'd like to run the simulation until N=10,000 (say) patients are recruited, and I'm interested in knowing how long that took (and after running the same simulations many hundreds of times, what the confidence interval is around expected enrollment length).

So I have a pre-defined schedule of "site" arrivals, each of which has it's own "patient" generation function, defined by the site's rate attribute. I understand I can use add_dataframe() to generate each site's arrival time, but I can't figure out how to get each site to then have it's own generator for patients? I get that I could have a separate patient generator for each site, and I can use activate() and set_source() to dynamically turn a site-specific generators on/off, but how do I dynamically figure out within the trajectory of a given site arrival which generator to activate and set the site-specific patient arrival rates, at run time?

My current stab (which of course doesn't work, since the function provided to add_generator is evaluated in the wrong environment for get_attribute() to work):

library(simmer)
library(magrittr)

env <- simmer("Patient Enrollment")

site_data <- data.frame(time=c(1,10,20), rate=c(2,1,5))

patient <- trajectory() %>%
  log_(function() paste0("patient enrolled: ", as.character(now(env))))

site <- trajectory() %>%
  log_(function() paste0("site startup: ",
                         as.character(now(
    env %<>% add_generator("patient", patient,
                                 function() rexp(1, get_attribute("rate")))
    ))))

env <- env %>%
  add_dataframe("site",
                site,
                site_data) %>%
  run() %>%
  wrap()
##
1: site0: site startup: 1
Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) :
  Evaluation error: no applicable method for 'get_attribute' applied to an object of class "character".

thanks again,
-Aaron
